message.content: {"caption":"Three-panel diagram comparing memory handling across a multi-session dialogue, a vanilla LLM, and an RL-finetuned LLM.","description":"The left panel, titled “Multi-session dialogues,” shows two conversations separated by a vertical dashed line labeled “Another day, new session.” In the first blue speech bubble, the user says, “Hi Audrey! I recently adopted a pup from a shelter. I named him Buddy.” A yellow reply says, “That's perfect, Andrew!” In the later blue bubble, the user says, “I can't help myself but to adopt another dog. His name is Scout.” The yellow reply says, “That's great news!” The middle panel, “Vanilla LLM as backbone,” starts with a purple box labeled “Current Memory Bank: Andrew adopted a new dog from a shelter and named him Buddy.” Below, the “In-context Memory Manager” is represented by a circuit-like brain icon and two red operation boxes: “DELETE: Andrew adopted a new dog from a shelter and named him Buddy.” and “ADD: Andrew adopted a new dog and named the pup Scout.” A red X marks this manager outcome. A horizontal dashed divider separates it from a retrieval box reading “Retrieved: <Memory 1> ... <Memory 60>” and “Question: How many dogs have Andrew adopted?” Below, “LLM generate response” accompanies another circuit-like brain icon and a red answer box, “Answer: 1 dog,” also marked with a red X. A red note says this misinterprets the different dog names as a conflict and overwrites the original memory. The right panel, “RL-finetuned LLM as backbone,” begins with the same purple current-memory box. Under “Memory Manager,” a database-and-robot icon accompanies a green box reading “UPDATE: Andrew adopted 2 dogs named Buddy and Scout.” A green check marks this outcome. Below a horizontal dashed divider, the retrieval box gives the same range of memories and question as the middle panel. The section “Answer Agent with Memory Distillation” shows a brain-and-robot icon and a green box reading “Useful memories for answering the question: <Memory 1> Answer: 2 dogs.” A green check marks the result. A green note says the second dog's name is interpreted as an addition and the memory is updated to reflect both adoptions. There are no arrows; the panels' vertical placement indicates the progression from dialogue or stored memory, through memory handling and retrieval, to an answer. The central comparison is that the vanilla system deletes and adds conflicting entries and answers “1 dog,” while the RL-finetuned system consolidates both adoptions and answers “2 dogs.”","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
